header.title: Muse semantic-content ontology
header.description: Ontology concepts for non-truth-valued discourse content and open semantic operators used by the learned semantic target.

definition.text: Focus operator adding the focused alternative, including source-grounded also/too readings.
Normative recommendation or advisability, including source-grounded advisory should readings.
Repetition/restoration operator contributed by source-explicit 'again'.
Temporal/aspectual operator contributed by a source-explicit 'already' reading without inventing an unexpressed presupposition formula.
Interrogative content explicitly offering proposition/content alternatives.
Dynamic modality expressing a participant's capability to realize the scoped proposition.
Directive content presented as a command.
Semantic content by which the presenter commits to a proposition/action rather than asserting its current truth.
A modal operator concerning permission, obligation, prohibition, or normative advisability.
Semantic content presented as a directive toward an addressee, distinct from asserting that its proposition already holds.
A modal operator grounded in properties or circumstances of a participant rather than information or norms.
An epistemic operator expressing source-grounded certainty or confidence without collapsing it to logical necessity.
Expectedness weaker than necessity, including source-grounded predictive should readings.
A modal operator concerning support, likelihood, or necessity relative to information or belief.
Epistemic necessity, as in a source-grounded must/cannot reading supported by information or inference.
Epistemic possibility, as in a source-grounded maybe/might reading.
Epistemic probability or likelihood, as in a source-grounded probably/likely reading.
An epistemic operator explicitly limiting an assertion to an information state, as in 'as far as we know'.
Focus operator expressing exclusion, including source-grounded only/merely/just readings.
Context-sensitive generalized quantifier expressing few domain members.
A source-grounded operator affecting focus alternatives without being reduced to cardinality.
A source-grounded quantifier operator whose force is not one of the closed exact logical/cardinality operators.
A propositional operator contributing generic or habitual force, distinct from universal quantification.
Semantic content whose discourse force requests resolution of an open or closed question rather than asserting a proposition.
Context-sensitive generalized quantifier expressing many domain members.
Optimization force such as source-explicit 'as many as possible' or 'as high ... as possible'.
Optimization force such as source-explicit 'as few as possible' or 'as low ... as possible'.
A propositional operator contributing modal force without conflating epistemic, deontic, and dynamic modality.
Generalized quantifier expressing most of the source-grounded domain.
Deontic obligation or requirement.
A propositional operator requiring source-explicit maximization or minimization relative to an expressed target, distinct from ordinary comparison or modality.
A propositional operator contributing source-explicit perfect aspect.
Deontic permission.
Interrogative content asking whether a proposition holds.
A propositional operator contributing source-explicit progressive aspect.
Deontic prohibition.
Commissive content presented as a promise.
A semantic operator whose scope is a proposition and whose subtype determines the operator force.
Semantic content that mentions or quotes exact source material without asserting the quoted material.
Directive content presented as a request.
Scalar focus operator such as source-grounded even.
An abstract content object presented by discourse without requiring that the content itself be truth-valued.
An abstract source-grounded semantic operator whose lexical identity is preserved when the distinction is not a closed logical connective.
Context-sensitive generalized quantifier expressing several domain members.
Temporal/aspectual continuation operator contributed by source-explicit 'still'.
Directive content presented as a suggestion or recommendation.
Interrogative content expressed by a source-explicit tag question construction.
A source-grounded propositional operator contributing temporal/aspectual meaning beyond tense.
Interrogative content binding one or more source-grounded answer variables.

sem:agentParticipant.definition: Relates an event or situation to a participant source-groundedly interpreted as agent/initiator.

sem:alternativeProposition.definition: Relates alternative-question content to one explicitly offered proposition alternative.

sem:beneficiaryParticipant.definition: Relates an event or situation to a participant source-groundedly interpreted as beneficiary.

sem:contentAddressee.definition: Relates semantic content to a source-established addressee/recipient without asserting the content proposition.

sem:contentParticipant.definition: Relates an event or situation to explicitly expressed semantic or informational content when no narrower ontology relation applies.

sem:contentPresenter.definition: Relates semantic content to a source-established presenter/sender without asserting the content proposition.

sem:contentProposition.definition: Relates semantic content to a proposition constituting its propositional body without asserting that proposition.

sem:epistemicSource.definition: Relates an epistemic operator to an explicitly expressed agent or source whose information state supplies the modal basis.

sem:experiencerParticipant.definition: Relates an event or situation to a participant source-groundedly interpreted as experiencer.

sem:explains.definition: Relates a proposition that supplies a source-explicit explanation or reason to the proposition it explains, without collapsing explanation into event causation.

sem:goalParticipant.definition: Relates an event or situation to an explicitly expressed goal/destination participant.

sem:instrumentParticipant.definition: Relates an event or situation to a participant source-groundedly interpreted as instrument.

sem:locationParticipant.definition: Relates an event or situation to an explicitly expressed location participant.

sem:operatorBearer.definition: Relates a scoped operator to an explicitly expressed bearer/subject when the operator's force is participant-relative, such as capability or obligation.

sem:optimizationTarget.definition: Relates an optimization operator to the source-grounded entity, variable, quality, or value dimension being maximized or minimized.

sem:patientParticipant.definition: Relates an event or situation to a participant source-groundedly interpreted as affected patient.

sem:questionAnswerVariable.definition: Relates interrogative content to a source-grounded typed variable whose value resolves part of the question. The variable carries its ontology domain independently.

sem:quotedText.definition: Relates quotation/mention content to the exact source text value it quotes or mentions without asserting that text as a proposition.

sem:recipientParticipant.definition: Relates an event or situation to a participant source-groundedly interpreted as recipient.

sem:sourceParticipant.definition: Relates an event or situation to an explicitly expressed source/origin participant.

sem:stimulusParticipant.definition: Relates an event or situation to a participant source-groundedly interpreted as stimulus.

sem:surfaceObjectParticipant.definition: Lowest-precision fallback preserving which participant is realized as the source clause object when no narrower semantic role is justified.

sem:surfaceSubjectParticipant.definition: Lowest-precision fallback preserving which participant is realized as the source clause subject when no semantic role is justified.

sem:themeParticipant.definition: Relates an event or situation to a participant source-groundedly interpreted as theme.
